 Kane and Putellas lift Ballon d'Or - plus all other award winners
 26 October 2026 Summary
 Harry Kane first English winner for 25 years and Alexia Putellas wins women's award
 Lamine Yamal and Vicky Lopez win young talent awards
 Perre Romeu and Luis de la Fuente awarded coach of the year
 Spain goalkeepers Cata Coll and Unai Simon win best goalkeepers
 Bukayo Saka wins Socrates award , which honours humanitarian work and social initiatives
 Barcelona women and Paris-St Germain win club of the year awards
 Harry Kane and Charlyn Corral win strikers of the year
 Kane announced as premature winner - but he wasn't only one 
 Close form Send us your views
 Get involved Live Reporting
 Gary Rose, George Booth and Keifer MacDonald

 'I've had to go through many ups and downs' published at 23:45 GMT 26 October 23:45 GMT 26 October 
 England 
 Some more words from Harry Kane, speaking to DAZN: “Not many people would have thought it and maybe even myself wouldn’t have thought I’d be this far. 
 “I had to go through many ups and downs, especially early in my career. I was never the person that people thought was going to be the superstar like some of the guys now. 
 “I had to bide my time and work hard, a lot of times it was me against my own mind and I had to come through it. I had to show self-belief, determination. I think that grounded me, even when I did make it at the highest level to keep improving and keep getting better. 
 “No matter what I achieve, how many goals I score, winning the Ballon d’Or, it's always about getting better. This is a showcase of that."

 'Brilliant player, remarkable captain' published at 23:42 GMT 26 October 23:42 GMT 26 October 
 Prince William has praised Harry Kane for being a "brilliant captain and remarkable player".
 He said: "Huge congratulations to Harry Kane on winning the Ballon d'Or! What a fantastic achievement and so deserved. 
 "A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments."

 'The home of the world's best footballer' published at 23:39 GMT 26 October 23:39 GMT 26 October 
 Image source, @england Wembley has been lit up to recognise Harry Kane's achievement, with the England X account writing: "The home of the world's best footballer."
 478 12 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'A huge honour' published at 23:37 GMT 26 October 23:37 GMT 26 October 
 England 
 England boss Thomas Tuchel has praised Harry Kane after his win: "I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I'm delighted to see that you have now been formally recognised by the football world.
 "To become the first Englishman to win this huge honour in 25 years makes it extra special and we are lucky to have you as our leader.
 "I know you will enjoy this moment with your loved ones and then get back to doing what you do best – scoring goals and winning football matches."

 'My kids back home watching - it's past your bedtime!' published at 23:06 GMT 26 October 23:06 GMT 26 October 
 England 
 Men's Ballon d'Or winner, Harry Kane thanking his family: "Thank you very much. I know how much support you give me. We all live these emotions together. I know how much help off the pitch, it allows me to perform and do my best on the pitch.
 "My brother Charlie, doesn't seem like long ago we were kicking a ball around the garden. Taking football, just football mad. I know you say you gave me your footballing ability, so thank you for that."Mum and dad - what a moment. All those years, the sacrifice, the support you gave me. Taking me to training, coming to watch me play. No matter where it was, even to this day you're there."All those traits you have given me have allowed me to be successful and be here tonight.
 "My kids back home watching - it is past your bedtime! You're the reason I do this. This one is a special one. I can't wait to see you and celebrate with you. I love you very much.
 "My wife Kate, my best friend. You're my biggest supporter. We have done it. You always want the best for me. You sacrifice yourself to help me achieve my dreams. It wouldn't be possible without you."

 Image source, EPA Coming towards the end of his speech and Harry Kane thanks his wife Katie.
 "We've done it, you always want the best for me and you sacrificed yourself to help me achieve my dreams and your dreams as well.
 "It would not be possible without you."

 Post published at 23:04 GMT 26 October 23:04 GMT 26 October

 Men's Ballon d'Or winner, Harry Kane paying his respects to all of his coaches: 
 "All of you played a big role in my development at different stages of my life. Without every single one of you I wouldn't be standing here today. I learnt lots. 
 "When you surround yourself with the best people - it only improves you as a person and as a player."
 3236 64 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Thank you to Tottenham' published at 23:02 GMT 26 October 23:02 GMT 26 October 
 England 
 Image source, Getty Images Men's Ballon d'Or winner, Harry Kane: "Thank you to Tottenham Hotspur as well. 
 "I wouldn't be where I am today without Tottenham. All the guidance, all the coaches you have allowed me to live my dream. For all those moments, all the ups and downs along the way has led me to this moment here today. 
 "To all the fans, Bayern, England fans, Spurs fans and all my fans around the world. I love you in this room tonight. 
 "The support you give me - I appreciate it all. I remember being a fan not long ago and what it means to play football. It was a dream of mine. 
 "Any time I can give back to you guys, it is an honour and privilege to do so."

 Post published at 23:00 GMT 26 October 23:00 GMT 26 October 
 Harry Kane is thanking everyone who has played their part in his career - from team-mates to coaches and to family. He is tearing up a bit as he thanks his parents.

 'An honour to captain England' published at 23:00 GMT 26 October 23:00 GMT 26 October 
 England 
 Image source, Getty Images Men's Ballon d'Or winner, Harry Kane: "To my England team-mates, again the same. 
 "We had a special year. It wasn't the perfect year, but we had a load of great moments. We built a great bond together. 
 "The togetherness in the hotel in the World Cup. An honour to captain you and lead you. It makes me extremely proud. This one is for all of us for sure. 
 "Thomas Tuchel and the staff at England, again, the leadership, the way you drive us, the way you push standards is something to be admired."
 5349 107 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Glad to be bringing the trophy back to Bayern Munich' published at 22:57 GMT 26 October 22:57 GMT 26 October 
 England 
 More from Men's Ballon d'Or winner, Harry Kane: "Without you guys [Bayern Munich team-mates] and the rest of the team, it wouldn't be possible, the way you guys push me, the way we compete.
 "So thank you very much. To Vinny [Vincent Kompany]. I know he is at home or still in the hospital. Wishing you well. I hope this gave you a bit of energy.
 "To all the staff, the way we train and the way you push us it is a credit to yourself.
 "Since I have been with you, I have improved as a player, improved as a person and a leader. Thanks to your leadership.
 "An honour to play for Bayern Munich. To represent you is a real privilege. Glad to be bringing this trophy back to Bayern Munich."
 5464 164 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 22:55 GMT 26 October 22:55 GMT 26 October 
 Image source, Getty Images England captain Harry Kane scored 73 goals across club and international competitions in the 2025-26 season. 
 While jurors are told to only take the most recent season into account when ranking players, Kane's astonishing 156 goals in 158 games for Bayern Munich since 2023 has lifted him to seventh in the German club's top scorer list. 
 He has led the Bundesliga's scoring charts for three consecutive seasons, as well as being Europe's top overall club goalscorer for 2025-26.
 Kane also led his country to their best World Cup finish since they won the tournament in 1966. England won the third-fourth place match to win a bronze medal and he finished fifth top scorer for the tournament.

 'Wow, wow, wow' published at 22:54 GMT 26 October 22:54 GMT 26 October 
 England 
 Image source, Getty Images Men's Ballon d'Or winner, Harry Kane: 
 "I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special. 
 "Made it a good omen for me tonight. Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was tough this year.
 "Some world-class players in the room tonight. Congratulations to all the winners and nominees tonight and impressive showing determination and hard work can really achieve."

 Image source, Getty Images Harry Kane takes it! 
 The England captain and prolific Bayern Munich striker is the Ballon d'Or winner, the first English man to win it in 25 years.
 Lots of cheers inside the auditorium as "Harry! Harry! Harry!" is chanted.
